Karthik / Aditya / Sean —

I pulled the sample profile and produced a first-pass sizing workbook (attached: dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx). High-level assumptions baked into the workbook:

- Traffic mix: 35% 8k, 65% 32k (matches Samir's note).
- Average tokens per request (inference tokens): 400 for 8k flows, 950 for 32k flows (these are post-prompt generation tokens).
- KV cache effectiveness: two modes modeled — OFF and ENABLED with prefix hit rate = 60% for repeat contexts (Vireo mentioned many batched analytics runs).
- Quantization profiles: FP16 baseline, INT8 optimized (we include quality regression risk note).
- Target latency SLO: 99th <= 250ms for 8k, <= 700ms for 32k (SLOs Vireo wants).

Summary recommendations (conservative, committed-month sizing):

- Baseline (FP16, KV OFF): 12 GPUs (A100-class) committed to hit SLOs with 20% headroom for steady-state. Peak burst guidance: +6 GPUs for 2–4 hours/day during nightly batch windows.

- KV ENABLED (FP16): 9 GPUs committed. KV caching reduces per-request memory and compute by ~22% for the observed mix due to fewer KV recomputations and reduced seq_len decode cost. Peak burst: +4 GPUs.

- INT8 + KV ENABLED (aggressive): 6 GPUs committed. INT8 reduces memory footprint and per-token compute enabling higher concurrency; downside: potential 0.5–1.5% generation quality regression on some instruction prompts — flagged for Vireo to evaluate. Peak burst: +3 GPUs.

Notes for procurement: committed counts above assume dedicated pool with persistent KV working set pinned to GPU memory (no offload). If the customer wants offload (host memory / NVMe) for cold KV partitions, we should discuss latency trade-offs and a different contract (sustained offload rate).

I've included a tab with per-model peak GPU residency (GiB) under each quant profile, and a tab that converts these to committed pod SKUs. Aditya — can you validate the memory residency numbers and add any kernel-level caveats?

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 184KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool sizing for our long-context models — technical validation

Team —

Validated Marissa's workbook and added engine-level caveats. Key technical calls:

- Memory residency per model (pinned, no offload):
  - vireo-large-32k (FP16): ~42 GiB model + ~28 GiB peak KV workspace = 70 GiB per GPU instance for single-concurrency hot-serving.
  - vireo-large-32k (INT8): ~31 GiB model + ~20 GiB KV workspace = 51 GiB per GPU.
  - vireo-base-8k (FP16): ~18 GiB model + ~6 GiB KV workspace = 24 GiB per GPU.
  - vireo-base-8k (INT8): ~14 GiB model + ~5 GiB KV workspace = 19 GiB per GPU.

- Concurrency and batching assumptions: we modeled 4 concurrent steady-state decoding streams per GPU for 32k on FP16, 6 streams on INT8 (due to lower mem/compute). For 8k flows we assumed 10 concurrent streams FP16, 14 on INT8. These drive the per-GPU throughput numbers in the workbook.

- KV prefix caching effect: with a 60% prefix hit rate, effective per-request KV recomputation drops ~45% overall because many requests reuse cached KV segments; this reduces both memory churn and kernel launch overhead. In practical terms: expect a 15–25% reduction in committed GPU count versus KV OFF for the Vireo mix.

- Quantization caveats: INT8 path relies on per-layer calibration and a small evaluation set. Some instruction-heavy prompts showed hallucination sensitivity in our internal tests; recommend a quality gate in production and a canary rollout (we can automate traffic-split).

- Operational ops note: If Vireo wants persistent KV pinned across restarts, we need disk-backed checkpointing and warm-up ramping. That adds ~10–15 minutes of warm start after instance replacement unless we use a shared in-memory KV store on a dedicated nodal pool.

My recommended conservative contract line items (for SOW):

- Committed pool: 9 x A100-equivalent GPUs (FP16, KV enabled) with a 20% guaranteed headroom clause.
- Optional upgrade: allow credit to convert to INT8-fast lane (reduce committed to 6 GPUs) after a successful canary (30 days).

I'll add the exact GiB numbers into the workbook's 'engine_notes' tab and a short checklist for canary validation metrics.

Aditya
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
